description: Chemotherapy regimen classification (anthracycline, taxane, platinum, alkylating, combination). Primary driver of treatment-induced neurotoxicity across multiple mechanistic pathways.
example_instruments: Clinical record extraction; ENUM {anthracycline_based, taxane_based, platinum_based, alkylating, antimetabolite, targeted_therapy, combination_chemo, none}

description: Radiation exposure type and location (cranial, whole-body, pelvic, none). Cranial radiation is strongest risk factor for direct CNS damage and BBB disruption.
example_instruments: Clinical record; ENUM {cranial, whole_brain, head_neck, thoracic, pelvic, none}

description: Current treatment phase. Drives prior selection (33 context-matched matrices) and modifier activation. Key variable for the 4-level fallback hierarchy in ALG-C1.
example_instruments: Patient/clinical report; ENUM {pre_treatment, active_treatment, early_recovery, late_recovery, long_term_survivorship}

description: Primary cancer diagnosis. Drives prior context matching and cancer-specific pathway activation patterns. Breast cancer has strongest evidence base; others use fallback priors.
example_instruments: Clinical record; ENUM {breast, colorectal, lung, prostate, hematological, gynecological, head_neck, brain_cns, pediatric_survivor, other}

description: Age at cancer diagnosis. Modifies neuroplasticity response (BDNF), neurogenesis capacity, and senescence baseline. Grade B modifier for multiple pathways. ACC formula uses max(1,(age-50)/10).
example_instruments: Patient report or clinical record; continuous 18-100

description: Biological sex. Modifies HPA axis reactivity and hormonal pathway effects. Relevant for endocrine therapy interactions (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors).
example_instruments: Patient report; ENUM {male, female, other}

description: APOE epsilon-4 carrier status. Grade A modifier (Pearce 2022). e4 carriers show attenuated exercise-cognition benefit and amplified neuroinflammatory response to chemotherapy.
example_instruments: Genetic test; ENUM {e4_homozygous, e4_heterozygous, non_carrier, unknown}

description: Premorbid cognitive reserve proxy based on education, occupation, and premorbid IQ. Grade B modifier (Stern 2009). m_CR in [0.7, 1.3]: >16yr edu → 0.7 (protective); <12yr → 1.3 (vulnerability).
example_instruments: Education years + occupation complexity; continuous composite or ordinal

description: Overall comorbidity burden (Charlson Comorbidity Index or count). Modifies metabolic pathway activation and vascular risk. Drives contraindication evaluation for exercise intensity.
example_instruments: Charlson Comorbidity Index or simple count; integer >=0

description: Weekly physical activity level. Primary intervention target for exercise interventions. Dose-response modeled via Emax/Hill functions (EC50 ~200 MET-min/wk for aerobic). Member of Fatigue-Activity feedback loop (LOOP_01).
example_instruments: IPAQ, GLTEQ, accelerometry, self-report MET-min/week

description: Sleep quality as a BEHAVIOR (sleep practices, hygiene). Distinct from NODE_SYM_SLEEP_DISRUPTION (the symptom). Target of CBT-I and sleep hygiene interventions. Drives glymphatic clearance pathway.
example_instruments: PSQI (inverted for POS_UP), sleep diary, actigraphy sleep efficiency

description: Dietary pattern quality (Mediterranean diet adherence, anti-inflammatory diet score). Targets neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, gut-brain axis, and metabolic pathways.
example_instruments: Mediterranean Diet Score, DASH score, Healthy Eating Index, food frequency questionnaire

description: Active stress management behavior (mindfulness, meditation, relaxation practice). Target of MBSR intervention. Modulates HPA axis and mood pathways.
example_instruments: Self-report practice frequency/duration, MBSR session completion

description: Social engagement and participation level. Drives cognitive stimulation through social interaction. Impacted by fatigue and depression (C5 pathway). Modulates neuroplasticity.
example_instruments: Lubben Social Network Scale, Social Activities Log, self-report frequency

description: Morning bright light exposure. Target of bright light therapy intervention (threshold model, -0.30 effect at >=20 min/day). Regulates circadian rhythm → sleep quality → HPA axis.
example_instruments: Self-report, lux meter, wearable light sensor; minutes of >10,000 lux within 2h of waking

description: Engagement in cognitively stimulating activities (cognitive training, reading, puzzles, learning). Target of cognitive rehabilitation interventions. Drives neuroplasticity and synaptic function.
example_instruments: Cognitive Activity Questionnaire, training program completion logs

description: Self-efficacy for behavior change and intervention adherence. Modulates actual adherence rates (P_adhere in SAFE score). Connected to dopaminergic motivation pathway. Impacted by fatigue and mood.
example_instruments: General Self-Efficacy Scale, Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale, treatment motivation VAS

description: Plasma IL-6 concentration. Primary peripheral proxy for neuroinflammation (OIC composite). Elevated by chemotherapy, reduced by exercise. Correlated with TNF-α (ρ=0.65), CRP (ρ=0.72).
example_instruments: INST_IL6_PLASMA (ELISA, plasma, fasting preferred)

description: High-sensitivity CRP (serum). Acute phase reactant downstream of IL-6. Less specific to neuroinflammation than IL-6 but more widely available clinically. Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.72).
example_instruments: INST_CRP_HS (hs-CRP, serum, immunoturbidimetric assay)

description: Plasma TNF-α. Pro-inflammatory cytokine linked to neuroinflammation and SASP (senescence-associated secretory phenotype). Drives cellular senescence pathway. Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.65), CRP (ρ=0.58).
example_instruments: INST_TNF_PLASMA (ELISA, plasma)

description: PLASMA BDNF (NOT serum — serum levels 20-200x higher due to platelet BDNF, confounding measurement). Primary proxy for neuroplasticity pathway. Increased by exercise, reduced by chronic stress. Anti-correlated with IL-6 (ρ=-0.35).
example_instruments: INST_BDNF_PLASMA (ELISA, plasma specifically, fasting, morning collection preferred; unit: pg/mL)

description: Salivary cortisol diurnal slope (>=2 days sampling). Flatter/less-negative slope indicates HPA dysregulation (POS_DOWN: higher raw value = flatter = worse). Primary proxy for HPA pathway. Requires multi-timepoint sampling (waking, +30min, afternoon, evening). Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.28).
example_instruments: INST_CORTISOL_SLOPE (salivary cortisol, 4-point diurnal, >=2 days)

description: T-cell p16^INK4a expression by flow cytometry. Primary peripheral proxy for cellular senescence. Elevated after chemotherapy, especially anthracyclines. Linked to accelerated cognitive aging.
example_instruments: INST_P16_TCELL (T-cell flow cytometry, quantitative RT-PCR)

description: Lymphocyte γ-H2AX foci count by immunofluorescence. Direct marker of DNA double-strand breaks. Elevated by chemotherapy and radiation. Primary proxy for DNA damage pathway.
example_instruments: INST_GH2AX_LYMPH (lymphocyte immunofluorescence microscopy)

description: Urinary or plasma 8-OHdG. Marker of oxidative DNA damage. Proxy for oxidative stress component of OIC composite. Elevated by chemotherapy-induced reactive oxygen species.
example_instruments: INST_8OHDG (ELISA, urinary preferred, plasma acceptable)

description: Plasma malondialdehyde. Lipid peroxidation marker for oxidative stress. Proxy for oxidative stress component of OIC composite. Correlation with IL-6 pending verification.
example_instruments: INST_MDA_PLASMA (TBARS assay or HPLC, plasma)

description: Fasting blood glucose. Proxy for metabolic dysregulation pathway. Insulin resistance impairs cerebral glucose metabolism and drives neuroinflammation. Elevated by dexamethasone and some chemotherapy regimens.
example_instruments: INST_GLUCOSE_FASTING (standard clinical lab, fasting, mg/dL or mmol/L)

description: Plasma neurofilament light chain. Marker of axonal/neuronal damage. CAUTION: Cannot distinguish CNS from PNS damage — elevated in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy independently of CRCI. Low proxy validity for BBB-specific damage.
example_instruments: INST_NFL_PLASMA (Simoa ultrasensitive immunoassay, plasma)

description: Shannon diversity index from 16S rRNA fecal sequencing. Proxy for gut-brain axis pathway. Reduced by chemotherapy and antibiotics. Limited cancer-specific normative data. Emerging biomarker with low proxy validity.
example_instruments: INST_SHANNON_16S (16S rRNA sequencing, fecal sample, Shannon H index)

description: COMPOSITE NODE absorbing M1 (Neuroinflammation) + M2 (Oxidative Stress) + M6 (Mitochondrial Dysfunction). Internal 3x3 covariance matrix + amplification factor α. Resolves bidirectional neuroinflammation ↔ oxidative stress ↔ mitochondrial dysfunction cycle within acyclic DAG. Best proxied by IL-6.
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_IL6 (primary), NODE_BIO_CRP, NODE_BIO_TNF, NODE_BIO_8OHDG, NODE_BIO_MDA

description: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation (M3). NIC covariance structure links this to OIC. Flattened cortisol slope indicates chronic stress response. Drives sleep disruption and mood disturbance. Proxied by cortisol diurnal slope.
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_CORTISOL (primary)

description: BDNF-mediated neuroplasticity (M4). Enhanced by exercise, suppressed by chronic inflammation and stress. Key pathway for exercise → cognition benefit. SE multiplier 1.15x (Moderate-High evidence, 1.5x in cancer-specific contexts).
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_BDNF (primary, PLASMA not serum)

description: Hippocampal adult neurogenesis (M5). BDNF-dependent. Exercise-promoted, chemotherapy-suppressed. Primary effect on episodic memory. Declines with age. No direct peripheral biomarker; inferred from BDNF + hippocampal volume (imaging).
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_BDNF (indirect), hippocampal volume on MRI if available

description: DNA damage and repair pathway (M7). Direct effect of chemotherapy and radiation. Drives cellular senescence via persistent damage foci. Proxied by γ-H2AX. Moderate-High evidence (1.15x SE multiplier).
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_GH2AX (primary)

description: Gut-brain axis dysfunction (M8). Chemotherapy-induced dysbiosis → increased intestinal permeability → systemic inflammation → neuroinflammation. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE multiplier). Proxied by Shannon diversity.
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_SHANNON (primary, low R²)

description: Cellular senescence and SASP (M9). Chemotherapy-induced senescent cell accumulation produces pro-inflammatory secretome. Drives accelerated cognitive aging. Proxied by p16^INK4a. Linked to ACC factor in temporal model.
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_P16 (primary)

description: Glymphatic waste clearance (M10). Sleep-dependent CNS waste clearance system. Sleep disruption → impaired glymphatic flow → neuroinflammatory metabolite accumulation. Part of LOOP_05 (HPA→Sleep→Glymphatic→Neuroinflammation→HPA). Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE).
example_instruments: Latent — no direct peripheral proxy. Inferred from sleep quality + neuroinflammation trajectory

description: Cerebrovascular function and perfusion (M11). EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER — pathway concept without parameterized edges in v1. Cerebral blood flow, endothelial function, vascular stiffness. Future expansion candidate.
example_instruments: Latent — no peripheral proxy. Would require TCD/MRI perfusion if available

description: Epigenetic modification pathway (M12). Chemotherapy-induced DNA methylation changes, histone modifications affecting gene expression in neuronal and glial cells. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE). No validated peripheral proxy for CNS epigenetic state.
example_instruments: Latent — no validated peripheral proxy. Research: global methylation, LINE-1

description: Metabolic dysregulation pathway (M13). Insulin resistance, impaired cerebral glucose metabolism. Dexamethasone and hormonal therapy can exacerbate. Links to neuroinflammation via metabolic inflammation. Proxied by fasting glucose.
example_instruments: Latent — proxied by NODE_BIO_GLUCOSE (primary), HbA1c, HOMA-IR if available

description: BBB disruption pathway (M14). EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER. Chemotherapy-induced BBB permeability allows peripheral inflammatory mediators into CNS. NfL is candidate proxy but cannot distinguish CNS from PNS damage. Future expansion candidate.
example_instruments: Latent — NODE_BIO_NFL (candidate proxy, low specificity). S100B, albumin quotient if CSF available

description: Synaptic function and long-term potentiation (M15). CONVERGENT HUB — receives input from neuroinflammation, BDNF, metabolic, and other pathways. Final common pathway before cognitive domains. 8 edges. No direct peripheral proxy.
example_instruments: Latent — no peripheral proxy. Inferred from convergent pathway structure

description: Myelin and oligodendrocyte integrity (M16). Chemotherapy directly toxic to oligodendrocytes → demyelination → processing speed deficits. Moderate-High evidence (1.15x SE). Primary effect on processing speed domain.
example_instruments: Latent — no peripheral proxy. DTI fractional anisotropy on MRI if available

description: Dopaminergic reward and motivation signaling (M17). Chemotherapy may disrupt dopamine synthesis/signaling → reduced motivation → reduced activity engagement → secondary cognitive effects. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE).
example_instruments: Latent — no peripheral proxy. Inferred from motivation/reward behavior patterns

description: Cancer-related fatigue severity. Most common CRCI comorbid symptom. Member of LOOP_01 (Fatigue ↔ Physical Activity, gain=0.16). Driven by neuroinflammation (OIC) and deconditioning. Directly impairs cognitive performance.
example_instruments: INST_FACIT_FATIGUE (primary), INST_BFI (alternative)

description: Depressive symptom severity. Member of LOOP_02 (Depression ↔ Sleep, gain=0.14). Part of CAL covariance structure (Cognitive-Affective Loop) with subjective cognition. PHQ-9 has known somatic confound in cancer (SE 1.5x).
example_instruments: INST_PHQ9 (with somatic confound warning), INST_PHQ2 (during active treatment)

description: Anxiety symptom severity. Member of LOOP_03 (Anxiety ↔ Sleep, gain=0.11). Driven by HPA dysregulation. Impairs attentional control and working memory through worry/rumination.
example_instruments: INST_GAD7 (primary)

description: Sleep disruption as SYMPTOM (distinct from NODE_BEH_SLEEP_QUALITY which is the behavior). Insomnia severity, fragmented sleep, non-restorative sleep. Member of LOOP_02 and LOOP_03. Impairs glymphatic clearance. Measured by ISI or PSQI component scores.
example_instruments: INST_ISI (primary for insomnia), INST_PSQI (sleep quality composite)

description: Pain severity (neuropathic and nociceptive). Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy is major contributor. Pain medications (opioids) independently impair cognition. Drives fatigue cycle.
example_instruments: INST_BPI (Brief Pain Inventory), NRS (Numeric Rating Scale), neuropathy grading

description: Patient-reported cognitive difficulties. Part of CAL covariance structure (correlated with depression — reporting bias). May exceed or underestimate objective cognitive impairment. Important for patient experience but not always correlated with neuropsych testing.
example_instruments: INST_FACTCOG_PCI (primary), INST_PROMIS_COG (PROMIS Cognitive Function)

description: Physical deconditioning and reduced cardiorespiratory fitness. Consequence of treatment-related fatigue → reduced activity → further deconditioning (vicious cycle). Reduced VO2max impairs cerebral blood flow and oxygen delivery.
example_instruments: 6MWT (6-Minute Walk Test), VO2max/peak, grip strength, self-reported functional status

description: Appetite disruption, nausea, weight changes. Chemotherapy-induced. Impacts nutritional status → gut microbiome → metabolic pathways. Particularly relevant during active treatment phase.
example_instruments: EORTC QLQ-C30 appetite items, CTCAE nausea grading, BMI change

description: Ability to maintain attention over time (vigilance). Commonly impaired in CRCI. Affected by fatigue, sleep disruption, and dopaminergic signaling.
example_instruments: CPT (Continuous Performance Test), sustained attention subtests

description: Ability to focus on relevant stimuli while filtering distractors. Impaired by anxiety (rumination occupies attentional resources) and neuroinflammation.
example_instruments: Stroop Test (color-word), Flanker Task, selective attention subtests

description: Speed of information processing. MOST SENSITIVE domain to chemotherapy effects (myelin/oligodendrocyte pathway M16). Often first deficit detected. Primary target of TMT-B, Digit Symbol.
example_instruments: INST_TMT_B (Trail Making B), WAIS Digit Symbol/Coding, Symbol Search

description: Ability to hold and manipulate information in short-term memory. Affected by neuroinflammation-mediated prefrontal cortex dysfunction. Linked to BDNF/neuroplasticity.
example_instruments: Digit Span Backward, N-back task, WAIS Working Memory Index

description: Ability to encode, store, and retrieve new information. Hippocampus-dependent. Most affected by neurogenesis pathway (M5) and BDNF (M4). Commonly reported CRCI complaint.
example_instruments: INST_HVLTR (Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised, primary), RAVLT, CVLT

description: Ability to generate words under constraint (phonemic and semantic). Requires processing speed + executive search + semantic memory. Sensitive to white matter integrity (myelin pathway).
example_instruments: FAS/COWAT (Controlled Oral Word Association Test), Animal Naming (semantic)

description: Executive function: planning, sequencing, and organization. Prefrontal cortex-dependent. Impaired by neuroinflammation-mediated PFC dysfunction. The paper splits executive function into planning and inhibition (2 nodes).
example_instruments: Tower of London, Trail Making B (planning component), WCST

description: Executive function: inhibitory control and response suppression. Dependent on prefrontal-striatal circuits. Linked to dopaminergic signaling (M17). Measured by Stroop interference, Go/No-Go.
example_instruments: Stroop Interference score, Go/No-Go task, Hayling Test

description: Visuospatial processing, construction, and mental rotation. Parietal cortex-dependent. Less commonly reported in CRCI but included for comprehensive cognitive assessment. MoCA includes visuospatial items.
example_instruments: Rey Complex Figure (copy), Block Design, Clock Drawing, MoCA visuospatial items

description: Language comprehension and expression beyond word retrieval (which is verbal fluency). Includes reading comprehension, sentence processing, discourse. Less commonly impaired in CRCI but relevant for functional assessment.
example_instruments: Boston Naming Test, Token Test, WAIS Comprehension, reading comprehension tasks

description: Severity-weighted inverse-variance average across L5 cognitive domains (Formula F-1). Weights w_d = 1/σ²_d. Severity weights 1.0x/1.5x/2.0x at z thresholds 1/2. Six tiers: Excellent(85-100)/Good(70-84)/Mild(50-69)/Moderate(30-49)/Poor(15-29)/Severe(0-14). Score = Φ(-z) × 100.
example_instruments: Computed by ALG-F1 from all L5 node values. Not directly measured.
